However, it tends to overestimate the true error in classification according to [Silke Janitza and Roman Hornung (2018)](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0201904){target="_blank"}. ::: ::: ::: ## [Bagging]{.blue}: [B]{.blue}ootstrap [Agg]{.blue}regat[ing]{.blue} ### Cool things in bagging/ random forest #### Feature Importances (FI) :::{style="font-size: 67%" .incremental} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="60%"} #### Mean Decrease in Impurity (MDI) - The [**R**]{.light-blue}eduction of [**I**]{.light-blue}mpurity [**M**]{.light-blue}easures when spliting at $X_j$ is denoted by $$\color{blue}{\text{RIM}}_t(X_j)=\text{Imp}_{t-1}(X_j)-\text{Imp}_t(X_j).$$ - The importance of feature $X_j$ within a tree: $\sum_{t\in S_j}\color{blue}{\text{RIM}_t(X_j)},$ where $S_j$ is the set of indices $t$ when a split is performed at $X_j$. - Unnormaized [**MDI**]{.light-blue} of variable $X_j$ is the sum of **FIs** from all the built trees. - ⚠️ Might be biased toward high cardinality features and might not be accurate with highly correlated features. ::: :::{.column width='40%' .fragment}

Schapire (1990)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00116037){target="_blank"}. - **Main framework:** Sequentially train a new weak learner to **correct mispredicted points** of the previous learners. The resulting model is the weighted average of all the trained learners. - **Form:** $\color{blue}{\hat{f}(x)=\sum_{t=1}^Tw_tf_t(x)}$ where $\color{blue}{f_t}$ are weak learners built on updated data $\color{blue}{D_t}$. - It focuses more on improving bias than the variance. ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### Algorithm :::{style="sont-size: 75%"} - Number of trees: $T$ - `for t = 1, 2,..., T`: - **Build weak learner** $f_t$ by minimizing error $\varepsilon_t$. - **Learn and ajust weights:** - Compute **learner weight** $w_t>0$ computed based on weighted data with weight $\{D_t(i):i=1,\dots,n\}$. - Compute **sample weight** $D_t(i)\to D_{t+1}(i)$ for obs $i$. - Combined model: $\color{blue}{\hat{f}(x)=\sum_{t=1}^Tw_tf_t(x)}$. ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### Algorithm :::{style="sont-size: 75%"} - Combined model: $\color{blue}{\hat{f}(x)=\sum_{t=1}^Tw_tf_t(x)}$. :::{.r-stack} ![](./img/boosting1.png){.fragment height="400" fig-align="center"} ![](./img/boosting2.png){.fragment height="400" fig-align="center"} ![](./img/boosting3.png){.fragment height="400" fig-align="center"} ![](./img/boosting4.png){.fragment height="400" fig-align="center"} ![](./img/boosting5.png){.fragment height="400" fig-align="center"} ::: ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### [Adaboost]{.blue}: [Ada]{.blue}ptive [Boost]{.blue}ing :::{style="font-size: 75%" .up1 .incremental} - It's for binary classification with $(\text{x}_i,y_i)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\{-1,1\},i=1,\dots,n$. - Initialize the [**sample weight**]{.purple}: $\color{purple}{D_1(i)=1/n}$ for all data point $\text{x}_i$. - `for t = 1, . . . , T:` - Train the base classifier $\color{blue}{f_t}$ by minimizing [$$\color{red}{\varepsilon_t}=\mathbb{P}(\color{blue}{f_t}(X)\neq Y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\color{purple}{D_t(i)}\mathbb{1}_{\{\color{blue}{f_t}(\text{x}_i)\neq y_i\}}.$$]{.br20} - Calculate the [**learner weight**]{.light-blue}: $\color{blue}{w_t}=\frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{1-\color{red}{\varepsilon_t}}{\color{red}{\varepsilon_t}}\right).$ - Update the [**sample weight**]{.purple} using $\color{purple}{D_{t+1}}=\frac{\color{purple}{D_t(i)}}{Z_t}e^{\color{blue}{-w_t}y_i\color{blue}{f_t}(\text{x}_i)}$ where $Z_t$ is the normalized constant. - **The final model**: $\color{blue}{\hat{f}}(\text{x}_0)=\text{sign}(\color{blue}{\sum_{t=1}^Tw_tf_t}(\text{x}_0))$. (**Read:** [Freund & Schapire (1999)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~yfreund/papers/IntroToBoosting.pdf){target="_blank" style="font-size:90%"}) ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### [XGBoost]{.blue}: E[X]{.blue}treme [G]{.blue}radient [Boost]{.blue}ing :::{style="font-size: 70%" .sbr .incremental} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="80%"} - It's a special case of [**Gradient Boosting**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06951){target='_blank'}: $F_M(\text{x})=\sum_{t=1}^Mw_tf_t(\text{x})$. - Let $L$ be the loss function of the problem: - Initial model: $F_0=\arg\min_{c}\sum_{i=1}^nL(y_i,c).$ - `for t = 1, 2, ..., M:` - Compute false residuals: $r_{t,i}=\frac{\partial L(y_i,f(\text{x}))}{\partial f(\text{x})}\Big|_{f(\text{x})=f_{t-1}(\text{x}_i)}$. - Train a base learner on the new data: $\{(\text{x}_i,y_i),r_{t,i}\}.$ - Solve for $\color{blue}{f_t}$ and $\color{blue}{w_t}$ from: $$(\color{blue}{w_t}, \color{blue}{f_t(\text{x})})=\arg\min_{\color{blue}{w,f}}\sum_{i=1}^nL(y_i,F_{t-1}(\text{x}_i)+\color{blue}{wf(\text{x}_i)}).$$ - [**Update the model:**]{.light-blue} $F_t(\text{x})=F_{t-1}(\text{x})+\color{blue}{w_tf_t(\text{x})}$. ::: :::{.column width="20%"} - In XGBoost: :::{style="font-size: 50%" .fragment} $$\begin{align*}L(F_t)&=\sum_{i=1}^nL(y_i,F_t(\text{X}_i))+\sum_{m=1}^t\Omega(f_m)\\ \Omega(f_t)&=\gamma T+\frac{1}{2}\lambda\|w\|^2.\\ L(F_t)&\approx \sum_{i=1}^n[g_iF_t(\text{x}_i)+\frac{1}{2}h_iF_t^2(\text{x}_i)]+\Omega(F_t),\\ g_i&=\frac{\partial L(y_i,F_t(\text{x}))}{\partial F_t(\text{x})}\|_{F_t(\text{x})=F_t(\text{x}_i)}\\ h_i&=\frac{\partial^2 L(y_i,F_t(\text{x}))}{\partial F_t(\text{x})^2}\|_{F_t(\text{x})=F_t(\text{x}_i)}. \end{align*}$$ :::{.hline} Read [Chen & Guestrin (1999)](https://www.kdd.org/kdd2016/papers/files/rfp0697-chenAemb.pdf){target="_blank"} ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### Have fun at 👉 [Gradient Boosting Playground](https://arogozhnikov.github.io/2016/07/05/gradient_boosting_playground.html){target='_blank'} ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### Other variants - `for t = 1, . . . , T:` - Train the base classifier $\color{blue}{f_t}$ by minimizing [$$\color{red}{\varepsilon_t}=\mathbb{P}(\color{blue}{f_t}(X)\neq Y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\color{purple}{D_t(i)}\mathbb{1}_{\{\color{blue}{f_t}(\text{x}_i)\neq y_i\}}.$$]{.br20} - Calculate the [**learner weight**]{.light-blue}: $\color{blue}{w_t}=\frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{1-\color{red}{\varepsilon_t}}{\color{red}{\varepsilon_t}}\right).$ - Update the [**sample weight**]{.purple} using $\color{purple}{D_{t+1}}=\frac{\color{purple}{D_t(i)}}{Z_t}e^{\color{blue}{-w_t}y_i\color{blue}{f_t}(\text{x}_i)}$ where $Z_t$ is the normalized constant. - **The final model**: $\color{blue}{\hat{f}}(\text{x}_0)=\text{sign}(\color{blue}{\sum_{t=1}^Tw_tf_t}(\text{x}_0))$. (**Read:** [Freund & Schapire (1999)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~yfreund/papers/IntroToBoosting.pdf){target="_blank" style="font-size:90%"}) ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### [XGBoost]{.blue}: E[X]{.blue}treme [G]{.blue}radient [Boost]{.blue}ing :::{style="font-size: 70%" .sbr .incremental} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="80%"} - It's a special case of [**Gradient Boosting**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06951){target='_blank'}: $F_M(\text{x})=\sum_{t=1}^Mw_tf_t(\text{x})$. - Let $L$ be the loss function of the problem: - Initial model: $F_0=\arg\min_{c}\sum_{i=1}^nL(y_i,c).$ - `for t = 1, 2, ..., M:` - Compute false residuals: $r_{t,i}=\frac{\partial L(y_i,f(\text{x}))}{\partial f(\text{x})}\Big|_{f(\text{x})=f_{t-1}(\text{x}_i)}$. - Train a base learner on the new data: $\{(\text{x}_i,y_i),r_{t,i}\}.$ - Solve for $\color{blue}{f_t}$ and $\color{blue}{w_t}$ from: $$(\color{blue}{w_t}, \color{blue}{f_t(\text{x})})=\arg\min_{\color{blue}{w,f}}\sum_{i=1}^nL(y_i,F_{t-1}(\text{x}_i)+\color{blue}{wf(\text{x}_i)}).$$ - [**Update the model:**]{.light-blue} $F_t(\text{x})=F_{t-1}(\text{x})+\color{blue}{w_tf_t(\text{x})}$. ::: :::{.column width="20%"} - In XGBoost: :::{style="font-size: 50%" .fragment} $$\begin{align*}L(F_t)&=\sum_{i=1}^nL(y_i,F_t(\text{X}_i))+\sum_{m=1}^t\Omega(f_m)\\ \Omega(f_t)&=\gamma T+\frac{1}{2}\lambda\|w\|^2.\\ L(F_t)&\approx \sum_{i=1}^n[g_iF_t(\text{x}_i)+\frac{1}{2}h_iF_t^2(\text{x}_i)]+\Omega(F_t),\\ g_i&=\frac{\partial L(y_i,F_t(\text{x}))}{\partial F_t(\text{x})}\|_{F_t(\text{x})=F_t(\text{x}_i)}\\ h_i&=\frac{\partial^2 L(y_i,F_t(\text{x}))}{\partial F_t(\text{x})^2}\|_{F_t(\text{x})=F_t(\text{x}_i)}. \end{align*}$$ :::{.hline} Read [Chen & Guestrin (1999)](https://www.kdd.org/kdd2016/papers/files/rfp0697-chenAemb.pdf){target="_blank"} ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### Have fun at 👉 [Gradient Boosting Playground](https://arogozhnikov.github.io/2016/07/05/gradient_boosting_playground.html){target='_blank'} ## Boosting {auto-animate="true"} ### Other variants -
